subject: Mathematics
title: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard & Basic Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: Number Systems (Real Numbers), Algebra (Polynomials, Linear Equations, Quadratic Equations, Arithmetic Progressions), Coordinate Geometry, Geometry (Triangles, Circles), Trigonometry, Mensuration (Areas, Volumes), and Statistics & Probability.
course_structure_overview: The CBSE Class 10 Mathematics examination assesses conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, mathematical reasoning, and problem-solving through real-world applications. The course integrates arithmetic, geometric, algebraic, and statistical methodologies.

units.name: Number Systems
chapters: Real Numbers (Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Proofs of Irrationality)

units.name: Algebra
chapters: Polynomials
Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
Quadratic Equations
Arithmetic Progressions (AP)

units.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters: Coordinate Geometry (Distance Formula, Section Formula)

units.name: Geometry
chapters: Triangles (Similarity, Basic Proportionality Theorem)
Circles (Tangents to a Circle)

units.name: Trigonometry
chapters: Introduction to Trigonometry
Trigonometric Identities (sin²θ + cos²θ = 1)
Heights and Distances (Angle of Elevation & Depression)

units.name: Mensuration
chapters: Areas Related to Circles
Surface Areas and Volumes (Combinations of Solids)

units.name: Statistics & Probability
chapters: Statistics (Mean, Median, Mode of Grouped Data)
Probability (Classical Approach)

typology.description: Recall facts, basic concepts, and state standard mathematical definitions.
Solve mathematical problems using acquired knowledge, facts, techniques, and rules.
Examine and break information into components, synthesize ideas, and solve multi-step problems.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: Minimum 50% competency-focused questions (MCQs, case-study questions, source-integrated assessments) in accordance with CBSE assessment reforms.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: No overall choice across the question paper; approximately 33% internal choices are provided across questions in all sections.

prescribed_books.title: Mathematics - Textbook for Class X
Guidelines for Mathematics Laboratory in Schools, Class X
Mathematics Exemplar Problems for Class X

breakdown.details: Continuous school-level periodic tests and diverse assessments (quizzes, oral tests).
Neatness, regular completion of classwork and homework assignments, student reflection.
Hands-on activities performed from the official NCERT Laboratory Manual.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Students must complete at least 10 hands-on math laboratory activities throughout the academic year to substantiate their internal assessment portfolio.

editorial_study_tips: Prioritize NCERT solved examples and textbook exercises before moving to secondary reference books.
Practice basic geometry theorems (especially the Basic Proportionality Theorem) with neat diagrams and formal statements.
Maintain a dedicated formula notebook for Surface Areas and Volumes, memorizing unit conversions carefully to avoid calculation errors.

subject: Science
title: CBSE Class 10 Science Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: Chemical Substances - Nature and Behaviour (Chemical Reactions, Acids/Bases/Salts, Metals/Non-metals, Carbon Compounds), World of Living (Life Processes, Control/Coordination, Reproduction, Heredity), Natural Phenomena (Light, Eye), Effects of Current (Electricity, Magnetism), and Natural Resources.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 Science develops fundamental scientific literacy across Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and Environmental Science, focusing on experimental observation, cause-and-effect reasoning, and real-world technology.

units.name: Chemical Substances - Nature and Behaviour
chapters: Chemical Reactions and Equations
Acids, Bases and Salts
Metals and Non-metals
Carbon and its Compounds

units.name: World of Living
chapters: Life Processes
Control and Coordination
How do Organisms Reproduce?
Heredity

units.name: Natural Phenomena
chapters: Light - Reflection and Refraction
The Human Eye and the Colourful World

units.name: Effects of Current
chapters: Electricity
Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

units.name: Natural Resources
chapters: Our Environment (Ecosystem, Ozone Depletion, Waste Management)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 39 Questions)

typology.description: Exhibit memory of previously learned material by recalling facts, terms, basic concepts, and demonstrating understanding.
Solve problems in new situations by applying acquired scientific knowledge, facts, techniques, and rules in different ways.
Examine and break information into parts, make inferences, construct explanations, and synthesize experimental conclusions.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-oriented questions including MCQs, Assertion-Reason questions, and Case-Based data interpretation problems.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of 33% are provided within designated short-answer and long-answer questions.

prescribed_books.title: Science - Textbook for Class X
Assessment of Practical Skills in Science - Class X
Laboratory Manual - Science - Class X
Exemplar Problems - Science - Class X

breakdown.details: Periodic pen-paper tests covering unit syllabus.
Quizzes, concept maps, and classroom oral assessments.
Maintenance of laboratory record book covering prescribed experiments and observation tables.
Student notebook, peer assessments, and project documentation.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Every student must perform the 14 officially prescribed core practicals (including Ohm's law, ray tracing through prisms, and stomata peel observation).

editorial_study_tips: Write balanced chemical equations with state symbols (s, l, g, aq) for full credit in inorganic and organic questions.
Draw ray diagrams for spherical mirrors and lenses strictly with arrowheads indicating light propagation direction.
Memorize all NCERT textbook diagrams in Biology (Nephron, Alimentary Canal, Reflex Arc, Heart) with exact labels.

subject: Social Science
title: CBSE Class 10 Social Science Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: History (India and the Contemporary World - II), Geography (Contemporary India - II), Political Science (Democratic Politics - II), and Economics (Understanding Economic Development).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 Social Science provides an integrated perspective on Indian history, world developments, physical geography, democratic institutions, and socio-economic dynamics.

units.name: India and the Contemporary World - II (History)
chapters: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
Nationalism in India
The Making of a Global World
The Age of Industrialization
Print Culture and the Modern World

units.name: Contemporary India - II (Geography)
chapters: Resources and Development
Forest and Wildlife Resources
Water Resources
Agriculture
Minerals and Energy Resources
Manufacturing Industries
Lifelines of National Economy

units.name: Democratic Politics - II (Political Science)
chapters: Power Sharing
Federalism
Gender, Religion and Caste
Political Parties
Outcomes of Democracy

units.name: Understanding Economic Development (Economics)
chapters: Development
Sectors of the Indian Economy
Money and Credit
Globalization and the Indian Economy

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 37 Questions)

typology.description: Factual recall of historical treaties, constitutional terms, geographic locations, and economic indices.
Explaining historical causes, comparative federal features, sectoral trends, and environmental policies.
Formulating arguments on democratic outcomes, economic disparities, and sustainable development.
2 marks History (Nationalism in India Congress sessions/centres) + 3 marks Geography (Dams, ports, airports, power plants).

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused items including case-based questions from source extracts.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choice of approximately 33% is provided in 3-mark and 5-mark subjective questions.

prescribed_books.title: India and the Contemporary World-II
Contemporary India-II
Democratic Politics-II
Understanding Economic Development

breakdown.details: Unit tests and continuous class assessments.
Classwork assignments, self-assessment, and map work practice files.
Individual student project on Consumer Awareness, Social Issues, or Sustainable Development.

practical_guidance.guidelines: The 5-mark project work must be handwritten and supported by primary or secondary research citations.

editorial_study_tips: Practice the official CBSE map items regularly on physical outline maps of India; map questions offer 5 guaranteed marks.
Structure 5-mark answers in point format with bold subheadings rather than uninterrupted paragraphs.
Remember that Economics definitions (e.g., Sustainable Development, Underemployment, Infant Mortality Rate) must adhere closely to NCERT wording.

subject: English Language & Literature
title: CBSE Class 10 English Language & Literature Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: Section A: Reading Skills (Discursive and Factual Passages); Section B: Writing Skills and Grammar (Formal Letters, Analytical Paragraphs, Tenses, Modals, Reported Speech); Section C: Prescribed Literature (First Flight and Footprints Without Feet).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 English Language and Literature builds communicative competence, reading comprehension, critical analysis of literary themes, and structured creative writing.

units.name: Reading Skills
chapters: Discursive Passage (400-450 words, 10 marks)
Case-Based Factual Passage with statistical data/charts (200-250 words, 10 marks)

units.name: Writing Skills and Grammar
chapters: Grammar: Tenses, Modals, Subject-Verb Concord, Reported Speech (10 marks)
Writing: Formal Letter on a given situation (5 marks)
Writing: Analytical Paragraph based on map/chart/graph/cue (5 marks)

units.name: Language through Literature
chapters: Reference to Context: One prose extract (5 marks) + One poetry extract (5 marks)
Short Answer Questions from First Flight (12 marks)
Short Answer Questions from Footprints Without Feet (6 marks)
Long Answer Question from First Flight (6 marks)
Long Answer Question from Footprints Without Feet (6 marks)

typology.description: Conceptual understanding, decoding, inferring, interpreting, and vocabulary analysis.
Creative expression, grammatical accuracy, structured paragraph formatting, and formal communication.
Literary analysis, character sketch, thematic interpretation, and extrapolative evaluations.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: Inferential and extrapolative questions testing deeper comprehension rather than rote summary memorization.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices provided in formal letter, analytical paragraph, and long literature questions.

prescribed_books.title: First Flight - Textbook for Class X
Footprints Without Feet - Supplementary Reader for Class X
Words and Expressions 2 - Workbook for Class X

breakdown.details: Evaluating comprehension of recorded audio passages and instructions.
Individual presentation, storytelling, or interactive viva conversation.
Continuous term evaluation and class notebook maintenance.

practical_guidance.guidelines: ALS is evaluated at the school level following standard CBSE rubrics for pronunciation, fluency, and vocabulary.

editorial_study_tips: Stick strictly to the 100-120 word limit for Formal Letters and Analytical Paragraphs to avoid deduction for extraneous length.
In literature answers, quote pivotal phrases or key terms from the text to demonstrate direct textual familiarity.
Practice editing and gap-filling grammar exercises daily to master subject-verb agreement and reported speech rules.

subject: Hindi Course-A
title: CBSE Class 10 Hindi Course-A Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: अपठित बोध (गद्यांश व काव्यांश), व्यावहारिक व्याकरण (रचना के आधार पर वाक्य भेद, वाच्य, पद-परिचय, अलंकार), पाठ्यपुस्तक क्षितिज भाग-2 व पूरक पाठ्यपुस्तक कृतिका भाग-2, तथा रचनात्मक लेखन (अनुच्छेद, पत्र, ई-मेल, विज्ञापन/सन्देश)।
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 Hindi Course-A strengthens linguistic proficiency in Hindi, covering literary appreciation of classic and modern Hindi literature, functional grammar, and creative compositions.

units.name: अपठित बोध
chapters: अपठित गद्यांश (चिंतन क्षमता एवं अभिव्यक्ति पर आधारित)
अपठित काव्यांश (काव्य सौंदर्य व भावबोध)

units.name: व्यावहारिक व्याकरण
chapters: रचना के आधार पर वाक्य भेद (4 अंक)
वाच्य: कर्तृवाच्य, कर्मवाच्य, भाववाच्य (4 अंक)
पद परिचय (4 अंक)
अलंकार: शब्दालंकार (श्लेष), अर्थालंकार (उत्प्रेक्षा, अतिशयोक्ति, मानवीकरण) (4 अंक)

units.name: पाठ्यपुस्तक व पूरक पाठ्यपुस्तक
chapters: क्षितिज भाग-2: गद्य खंड (14 अंक)
क्षितिज भाग-2: काव्य खंड (14 अंक)
कृतिका भाग-2: पूरक पाठ्यपुस्तक प्रश्न (6 अंक)

units.name: रचनात्मक लेखन
chapters: अनुच्छेद लेखन (6 अंक)
औपचारिक / अनौपचारिक पत्र लेखन (5 अंक)
स्ववृत्त लेखन अथवा ई-मेल लेखन (5 अंक)
विज्ञापन लेखन अथवा संदेश लेखन (4 अंक)

typology.description: गहन पठन, भाव ग्रहण और विश्लेषण पर आधारित बहुविकल्पी प्रश्न।
व्याकरणिक नियमों का सटीक अनुप्रयोग व भेद पहचान।
क्षितिज व कृतिका के पाठों के आधार पर विचार व मूल्यपरक प्रश्न।
सटीक प्रारूप, विषयवस्तु व भाषाई शुद्धता आधारित लेखन।

question_paper_design.competency_focus: दक्षता-आधारित प्रश्न (लगभग 50%), जिसमें स्थिति-आधारित अनुच्छेद व व्यावहारिक व्याकरण शामिल हैं।
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: रचनात्मक लेखन तथा पाठ्यपुस्तक आधारित प्रश्नों में पर्याप्त आंतरिक विकल्प उपलब्ध हैं।

prescribed_books.title: क्षितिज भाग-2
कृतिका भाग-2

breakdown.details: विद्यालय स्तरीय आवधिक परीक्षाएं।
कक्षा कार्य, प्रश्नोत्तरी व मौखिक प्रस्तुतियां।
अभ्यास पुस्तिका का रख-रखाव व नियमितता।
हिंदी उच्चारण, धाराप्रवाह वाचन व श्रवण बोध।

practical_guidance.guidelines: श्रवण व वाचन कौशल का मूल्यांकन बोर्ड द्वारा निर्धारित मानकों के अनुसार विद्यालय स्तर पर किया जाता है।

editorial_study_tips: व्याकरण के चारों विषयों (वाक्य भेद, वाच्य, पद परिचय, अलंकार) के नियमों का अभ्यास नियमित लिखित उदाहरणों के साथ करें।
रचनात्मक लेखन (पत्र, विज्ञापन, ई-मेल) में निर्धारित प्रारूप (Format) का विशेष ध्यान रखें, क्योंकि प्रारूप के निर्धारित अंक होते हैं।
क्षितिज के पद्य खंड में कविताओं के केंद्रीय भाव व रूपक-प्रतीकों को बिंदुवार समझें।

subject: Computer Applications
title: CBSE Class 10 Computer Applications Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Class X curriculum: Unit 1: Networking (Internet, Web Services, Protocols); Unit 2: HTML (Forms, CSS styling, Tables, Links); Unit 3: Cyber Ethics (Netiquette, Software licenses, Digital property rights, Secure browsing); and practical lab assignments.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 Computer Applications introduces practical computer ethics, standard web page authoring using HTML/CSS, and foundational cyber security practices.

units.name: Networking
chapters: Internet: World Wide Web, web servers, clients, browsers, blogs, URLs, search engines
Internet protocols: TCP/IP, SMTP, POP3, HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, SFTP, FTP, TELNET
Web services: chat, email, video conferencing, e-Learning, e-Banking, e-Shopping, e-Governance, social networks
Mobile technologies: SMS, MMS, 3G, 4G, 5G

units.name: HTML
chapters: Basic HTML tags: html, head, title, body, headings, paragraphs, br, hr
Lists: ordered, unordered, definition lists
Images, Hyperlinks (internal and external), Audio/Video embedding
Tables: table, tr, th, td, colspan, rowspan
HTML Forms: text box, radio buttons, checkbox, password, submit, combo box
Cascading Style Sheets (CSS): inline, embedded, external styles

units.name: Cyber ethics
chapters: Netiquettes and digital footprint
Software licenses and Open Source software movement
Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), plagiarism, digital property rights
Freedom of information and the digital divide
E-commerce: privacy, fraud, secure data transmission

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (50 Marks, 2 Hours) + Practical Exam (50 Marks)

typology.description: Definitions of internet terms, cyber laws, HTML tag syntax, and cyber security concepts.
Writing HTML code snippets, designing tables, formatting web pages, and correcting code errors.
Scenario-based questions assessing safe digital conduct and incident handling.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: Practical application of HTML/CSS code syntax and ethical problem-solving.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices provided in subjective HTML coding questions.

prescribed_books.title: Computer and Communication Technology - Class X
CBSE Curriculum Document for Computer Applications (Subject Code 165)

breakdown.item: Lab Test (HTML & CSS Web Page Design)
breakdown.details: On-screen authoring of an interactive HTML web page with styling, tables, and forms.
Minimum 10 practical HTML programs compiled and validated.
Oral questions on web standards, tag attributes, and cyber safety practices.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Practical examinations are evaluated internally by the school under standard board criteria.

editorial_study_tips: Practice writing HTML code by hand on paper without auto-completion to build muscle memory for opening and closing tags.
Double-check table attributes (`colspan`, `rowspan`) through pencil sketches before writing code.
Be clear on differences between Proprietary Software, Freeware, Shareware, and Free & Open Source Software (FOSS).

subject: Artificial Intelligence
title: CBSE Class 10 Artificial Intelligence Syllabus (2026-27)
description: CBSE Secondary Skill Subject: Introduction to AI, AI Project Cycle, Advance Python, Data Science, and Computer Vision. (Current Class 10 document link is unverified because the official CBSE catalog currently lists only the Class IX PDF 417-AI-IX.pdf).
verification_note: Current syllabus link not verified yet. CBSE 2026-27 curriculum directory currently lists only the Class IX document (417-AI-IX.pdf) for this skill subject. Class 10 link not published separately.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 10 Artificial Intelligence (Subject Code 417) is an elective skill curriculum designed to introduce foundational concepts of AI ethics, data science, computer vision, and natural language processing.

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (50 Marks) + Practical Assessment (50 Marks) — Note: Official Session Syllabus Link Unverified
question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50 Marks Theory + 50 Marks Practical framework as per standard CBSE Skill Education guidelines.

prescribed_books.title: CBSE Skill Education Facilitator Handbook - Artificial Intelligence Class X

breakdown.details: Practical test on Python AI scripts, mini-project, and logbook.
Oral viva on AI project cycle and practical implementation.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Subject to official verification on cbseacademic.nic.in/skill-education.html.

editorial_study_tips: Consult the official CBSE Skill Education portal directly for confirmed curriculum blueprints before purchasing third-party guides.
Focus on the AI Project Cycle (Problem Scoping, Data Acquisition, Data Exploration, Modelling, Evaluation) as foundational theory.
Practice core Python syntax (loops, conditionals, lists, and basic math operations) for practical lab evaluation.

subject: Physics
title: CBSE Class 12 Physics Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Electrostatics, Current Electricity, Magnetic Effects of Current & Magnetism, EMI & AC, Electromagnetic Waves, Optics, Dual Nature of Radiation & Matter, Atoms & Nuclei, and Semiconductor Electronics.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Physics emphasizes rigorous conceptual reasoning, mathematical formulations, experimental inquiry, and technological applications across classical electromagnetism, modern physics, and electronic devices.

units.name: Electrostatics & Current Electricity
chapters: Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields
Chapter 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
Chapter 3: Current Electricity

units.name: Magnetic Effects of Current & EMI / AC
chapters: Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism
Chapter 5: Magnetism and Matter
Chapter 6: Electromagnetic Induction
Chapter 7: Alternating Current

units.name: Electromagnetic Waves & Optics
chapters: Chapter 8: Electromagnetic Waves
Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
Chapter 10: Wave Optics

units.name: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms & Nuclei
chapters: Chapter 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
Chapter 12: Atoms
Chapter 13: Nuclei

units.name: Electronic Devices
chapters: Chapter 14: Semiconductor Electronics (Materials, Devices, and Simple Circuits)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (70 Marks, 3 Hours, 33 Questions)

typology.description: State scientific laws, define physical quantities, state SI units, explain fundamental derivations.
Formulate and solve numerical problems, trace ray diagrams, design circuit configurations.
Interpret graphical data, reason through complex electromagnetic scenarios, and solve case-based questions.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-based questions including Assertion-Reasoning and Case-Based data scenarios.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: No overall choice; internal choices of 33% are provided in 2-mark, 3-mark, and 5-mark questions.

prescribed_books.title: Physics Part-I, Class XII
Physics Part-II, Class XII
Laboratory Manual of Physics, Class XII
Exemplar Problems in Physics, Class XII

breakdown.item: Two Experiments (One from Section A, One from Section B)
breakdown.details: 7 marks per experiment evaluated on circuit setup/ray alignment, observations, and calculations.
Neat documentation of at least 8 experiments and 6 activities performed throughout the session.
Written project report on an applied physics topic with working demonstration or model.
Oral questions on theory, experimental procedures, errors, and investigatory project.
Demonstration of one activity from each section.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Practical exams are conducted under the supervision of an external examiner appointed by CBSE.

editorial_study_tips: Master standard derivations (Gauss's law applications, Lens Maker's formula, Young's double slit interference, AC generator) with clean labeled diagrams.
Always state the standard SI unit with every final numerical answer; half-mark penalties apply for missing units.
Practice drawing and analyzing graphs (e.g., photo-electric current vs frequency, semiconductor I-V curves, binding energy curve).

subject: Chemistry
title: CBSE Class 12 Chemistry Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Solutions, Electrochemistry, Chemical Kinetics, d- and f-Block Elements, Coordination Compounds, Haloalkanes & Haloarenes, Alcohols/Phenols/Ethers, Aldehydes/Ketones/Carboxylic Acids, Amines, and Biomolecules.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Chemistry provides deep conceptual grounding in physical chemistry principles, inorganic coordination compounds and d/f-block metals, and systematic organic reaction mechanisms and biomolecules.

units.name: Solutions
chapters: Types of solutions, Colligative properties, Raoult's law, Van 't Hoff factor

units.name: Electrochemistry
chapters: Redox reactions, Nernst equation, Conductance, Kohlrausch's law, Batteries & Fuel cells

units.name: Chemical Kinetics
chapters: Rate of reaction, Order & Molecularity, Integrated rate equations, Arrhenius equation

units.name: d- and f-Block Elements
chapters: Transition elements, Electronic configuration, Lanthanoids & Actinoids, Potassium dichromate/permanganate

units.name: Coordination Compounds
chapters: Werner's theory, IUPAC nomenclature, Isomerism, Valence Bond Theory, Crystal Field Theory

units.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
chapters: Nomenclature, Nature of C-X bond, SN1 and SN2 mechanisms, Optical rotation

units.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
chapters: Nomenclature, Preparation methods, Physical and chemical properties, Mechanism of dehydration

units.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
chapters: Carbonyl group, Nucleophilic addition mechanisms, Aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, Acidity

units.name: Amines
chapters: Classification, Basic character of amines, Diazonium salts and synthetic transformations

units.name: Biomolecules
chapters: Carbohydrates (monosaccharides, disaccharides), Proteins (peptide bond, denaturation), Nucleic acids

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (70 Marks, 3 Hours, 33 Questions)

typology.description: State chemical laws, IUPAC nomenclature, periodic trends, electronic configurations, and reagent roles.
Solve numericals on electrochemistry and kinetics; predict reaction products and conversion pathways.
Reasoning questions on organic reaction mechanisms, anomalous transition metal properties, and case-studies.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including reasoning MCQs and data-oriented passage questions.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% provided across sections.

prescribed_books.title: Chemistry Part-I, Class XII
Chemistry Part-II, Class XII
Laboratory Manual of Chemistry, Class XII

breakdown.details: Standard solution preparation and redox titration of KMnO4 against oxalic acid or Mohr's salt.
Detection of one cation and one anion in an unknown inorganic salt.
Chromatography, preparation of inorganic/organic compounds, or tests for functional groups.
Investigatory project report on an applied chemical phenomenon.
Regularity of practical notebook and viva voce by external examiner.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Practical evaluation is conducted jointly by an external examiner appointed by CBSE and an internal examiner.

editorial_study_tips: Write organic named reactions (Reimer-Tiemann, Kolbe, Aldol, Cannizzaro, Hoffmann bromamide) on flashcards and review weekly.
In Physical Chemistry numericals (Nernst equation, first-order kinetics), show step-by-step substitution with logarithmic calculations.
Focus on the reasons behind transition metal trends (variable oxidation states, catalytic behavior, colored ions) using exact NCERT explanations.

subject: Biology
title: CBSE Class 12 Biology Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Reproduction (Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Human Reproduction, Reproductive Health), Genetics and Evolution, Biology and Human Welfare, Biotechnology and Its Applications, Ecology and Environment.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Biology explores human and plant reproduction, principles of genetics and modern molecular biology, biotechnology tools, human health, and ecosystem ecology.

units.name: Reproduction
chapters: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
Human Reproduction
Reproductive Health

units.name: Genetics and Evolution
chapters: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
Molecular Basis of Inheritance
Evolution

units.name: Biology and Human Welfare
chapters: Human Health and Diseases
Microbes in Human Welfare

units.name: Biotechnology and Its Applications
chapters: Biotechnology - Principles and Processes (Recombinant DNA technology)
Biotechnology and its Applications (Medicine, Agriculture)

units.name: Ecology and Environment
chapters: Organisms and Populations
Ecosystem
Biodiversity and Its Conservation

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (70 Marks, 3 Hours, 33 Questions)

typology.description: State, name, list, identify, define, suggest, describe, outline, and summarize biological phenomena, systems, and principles.
Calculate, illustrate, show, adapt, explain, and distinguish biological concepts, pedigree charts, and biotechnological processes.
Interpret, analyse, compare, contrast, examine, evaluate, discuss, and construct biological insights and experimental observations.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-oriented questions including Assertion-Reasoning and Case-Based scenarios.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% are provided in 2-mark, 3-mark, and 5-mark questions.

prescribed_books.title: Biology, Class XII
Laboratory Manual of Biology, Class XII

breakdown.details: Isolate DNA from available plant material, pollen germination, or soil/water analysis.
Transpiration setup, population density by quadrat method.
Temporary mount preparation (pollen tube growth or onion root tip for mitosis).
Identification of biological specimens, prepared slides, and ecological models.
Laboratory record file and oral viva voce.
Investigatory project file and discussion.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Conducted with an external examiner appointed by CBSE.

editorial_study_tips: Draw and label genetic and physiological diagrams (lac operon, tRNA structure, pBR322 vector, human gametogenesis) repeatedly.
Memorize all phenotypic and genotypic ratios for monohybrid, dihybrid, incomplete dominance, and codominance crosses.
In ecology and environmental questions, write point-wise answers that integrate standard NCERT ecological terms and graphs.

subject: Mathematics
title: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Relations and Functions, Algebra (Matrices, Determinants), Calculus (Continuity, Differentiability, Integrals, Differential Equations), Vectors & 3D Geometry, Linear Programming, and Probability.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics covers relations and matrices, rigorous single-variable differential and integral calculus, 3D vector geometry, linear programming, and conditional probability.

units.name: Relations and Functions
chapters: Relations and Functions (Equivalence relations, One-one and onto functions)
Inverse Trigonometric Functions

units.name: Algebra
chapters: Matrices (Operations, Transpose, Symmetric/Skew-symmetric)
Determinants (Adjoint, Inverse, System of linear equations)

units.name: Calculus
chapters: Continuity and Differentiability (Chain rule, Logarithmic differentiation)
Applications of Derivatives (Rate of change, Increasing/Decreasing, Maxima/Minima)
Integrals (Definite & Indefinite integrals, Properties of definite integrals)
Applications of Integrals (Area under simple curves)
Differential Equations (Separable variables, Homogeneous, Linear differential equations)

units.name: Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry
chapters: Vectors (Dot product, Cross product)
Three-Dimensional Geometry (Direction cosines/ratios, Equation of line, Skew lines, Shortest distance)

units.name: Linear Programming
chapters: Linear Programming (Mathematical formulation, Graphical method, Corner point method)

units.name: Probability
chapters: Conditional Probability, Multiplication theorem, Bayes' Theorem, Random variables

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 38 Questions)

typology.description: Formulate mathematical concepts, evaluate basic matrices, apply fundamental calculus theorems.
Solve multi-step integration problems, find shortest distance between lines, apply Bayes' theorem.
Real-world optimization problems (maxima/minima word problems) and case-based application questions.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including MCQs and Case-Based scenarios.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% are provided across 2-mark, 3-mark, and 5-mark questions.

prescribed_books.title: Mathematics Part I, Class XII
Mathematics Part II, Class XII
Laboratory Manual of Mathematics, Class XII

breakdown.details: Best two out of three periodic pen-paper tests held across the session.
10 hands-on math laboratory activities documented in practical notebook, plus year-end assessment.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Assessed at the school level using CBSE's continuous assessment manual.

editorial_study_tips: Calculus accounts for 35 out of 80 marks; dedicate at least 45% of your regular revision time to mastering definite integral properties and maxima/minima applications.
Write complete step-by-step justifications in matrix inversion and linear programming; partial marks are strictly awarded for each verified stage.
In 3D Geometry, clearly define vector coordinates before calculating the shortest distance between skew lines.

subject: Computer Science
title: CBSE Class 12 Computer Science (Python) Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Computational Thinking and Programming - 2 (Python functions, file handling, data structures), Computer Networks, and Database Management (SQL interface and Python connectivity).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Computer Science develops computational problem-solving using Python 3, object manipulation, file persistence, network fundamentals, and relational database management using SQL.

units.name: Computational Thinking and Programming - 2
chapters: Revision of Python basics, Functions (arguments, scope)
Exception Handling (try-except blocks)
File Handling: Text files, Binary files (pickle module), CSV files (csv module)
Data Structures: Linear list implementation of Stack (push, pop)

units.name: Computer Networks
chapters: Evolution of networking, Data communication terminology, Transmission media
Network devices (hub, switch, router, gateway), Topologies (bus, star)
Network Protocols (HTTP, FTP, PPP, SMTP, POP3), Web services and Cloud concepts

units.name: Database Management
chapters: Database concepts, Relational Data Model, SQL DDL/DML commands
Constraints (Primary Key, Foreign Key, Not Null, Unique, Default)
SQL Functions (Aggregate, String, Date, Math), Group By, Having, Joins
Interface Python with SQL database using mysql.connector

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (70 Marks, 3 Hours, 35 Questions)

typology.description: Python syntax rules, network definitions, SQL clause functions, and data structure principles.
Writing Python functions, binary/text file operations, stack algorithms, and complex SQL query drafting.
Network layout design for institutional campuses and database-Python integration scripts.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including code output tracing, error finding, and case-based network layout questions.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of 33% provided across programming and SQL sections.
question_paper_design.editorial_notice: CBSE does not publish an official cognitive percentage table for Computer Science (Code 083) in the 2026-27 curriculum. The percentages below represent StudySignal editorial estimates to assist students with balanced study planning across programming, database, and networking sections.

prescribed_books.title: Computer Science with Python, Class XII
CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum Document for Computer Science (Code 083)

breakdown.details: Writing and executing a Python program demonstrating file handling or stack implementation.
Writing and executing SQL queries based on a given database schema.
Minimum 15 Python programs and 5 SQL queries properly documented with outputs.
Collaborative real-world application developed using Python and SQL database connectivity.
Oral questions on Python libraries, database commands, and project code.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Conducted with an external examiner appointed by CBSE.

editorial_study_tips: In file handling, memorize syntax for `pickle.dump()` and `pickle.load()` with proper exception handling (`EOFError`).
In SQL queries, distinguish carefully between `WHERE` and `HAVING` filters; `HAVING` must only be used with aggregate functions.
For campus network layout questions, place the server in the building with the maximum number of computers to minimize cable length.

subject: Accountancy
title: CBSE Class 12 Accountancy Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Accounting for Partnership Firms (Admission, Retirement, Death, Dissolution), Accounting for Companies (Share Capital & Debentures), Financial Statement Analysis, and Cash Flow Statement.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Accountancy provides thorough vocational knowledge of corporate accounting, partnership reconstructions, company share issues, debenture redemption, and statutory financial statement analysis.

units.name: Accounting for Partnership Firms and Companies
chapters: Unit 1: Accounting for Partnership Firms - Fundamentals, Goodwill, Change in PSR, Admission, Retirement/Death, Dissolution (36 marks)
Unit 2: Accounting for Companies - Issue of Shares, Forfeiture & Reissue, Issue of Debentures (24 marks)

units.name: Financial Statement Analysis
chapters: Unit 3: Analysis of Financial Statements - Financial Statements of a Company, Financial Statement Analysis Tools, Accounting Ratios (12 marks)
Unit 4: Cash Flow Statement - AS-3 Indirect Method (8 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 34 Questions)

typology.description: State statutory accounting rules, partnership provisions, company acts, and ratio formulas.
Prepare journal entries for share forfeiture/reissue, revaluation accounts, and partner capital accounts.
Comprehensive cash flow statements, ratio analysis interpretations, and dissolution realization accounts.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including real-world corporate balance sheet scenarios.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of 33% are provided across questions in both Part A and Part B.

prescribed_books.title: Accountancy: Partnership Accounts Part-I, Class XII
Accountancy: Company Accounts & Analysis Part-II, Class XII

breakdown.details: Comprehensive project file covering business transactions, journal entries, ledger accounts, trial balance, and financial statement analysis.
Oral viva voce conducted by an external examiner appointed by CBSE based on the submitted project file.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Evaluated jointly by an external examiner appointed by CBSE and the internal subject teacher.

editorial_study_tips: Always include concise narrations in all journal entries; marks are deducted for missing narrations in board exams.
In share capital, master the pro-rata allotment table to calculate excess application money transferred to allotment.
In Cash Flow Statements, ensure non-cash and non-operating items (depreciation, gain/loss on asset sale) are correctly classified in Operating Activities.

subject: Business Studies
title: CBSE Class 12 Business Studies Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Principles and Functions of Management (Planning, Organizing, Staffing, Directing, Controlling), Business Finance, Financial Markets, Marketing Management, and Consumer Protection.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Business Studies covers principles and operational functions of management, corporate finance, capital markets, marketing mix strategies, and consumer rights under the Consumer Protection Act.

units.name: Principles and Functions of Management
chapters: Nature and Significance of Management, Principles of Management, Business Environment (16 marks)
Planning and Organising (14 marks)
Staffing, Directing, and Controlling (20 marks)

units.name: Business Finance and Marketing
chapters: Financial Management and Financial Markets (15 marks)
Marketing Management and Consumer Protection (15 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 34 Questions)

typology.description: Exhibit memory of learned material by recalling facts, terms, basic concepts, and stating main management principles and processes.
Solve problems to new situations by applying acquired management knowledge, leadership principles, techniques, and rules in business scenarios.
Examine business case problems, evaluate financial decisions, compare market options, and formulate strategic recommendations.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions, dominated by scenario-based case studies.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices provided in 3-mark, 4-mark, and 6-mark questions.

prescribed_books.title: Business Studies Part I: Principles and Functions of Management
Business Studies Part II: Business Finance and Marketing

breakdown.details: Handwritten investigation on one of the four CBSE topics: Elements of Business Environment, Principles of Management, Stock Exchange, or Marketing.
In-depth oral examination on the project file and conceptual business foundations.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Evaluated by a CBSE-appointed external examiner.

editorial_study_tips: In case-study questions, read the final question prompt first before reading the paragraph to identify what concept is being targeted.
Always quote lines from the case study extract to substantiate your identification of the management principle or function.
Memorize the 4Ps of marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) and their individual components with practical examples.

subject: Economics
title: CBSE Class 12 Economics Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Part A: Introductory Macroeconomics (National Income Accounting, Money and Banking, Determination of Income and Employment, Government Budget, Balance of Payments). Part B: Indian Economic Development.
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Economics integrates aggregate macroeconomics (national income accounting, central banking, fiscal policy) with a historical and contemporary analysis of Indian economic development.

units.name: Introductory Macroeconomics
chapters: National Income and Related Aggregates (10 marks)
Money and Banking (6 marks)
Determination of Income and Employment (12 marks)
Government Budget and the Economy (6 marks)
Balance of Payments and Foreign Exchange (6 marks)

units.name: Indian Economic Development
chapters: Development Experience (1947-90) & Economic Reforms since 1991 (12 marks)
Current Challenges facing Indian Economy: Human Capital, Rural Development, Employment, Sustainable Development (20 marks)
Development Experience of India: A Comparison with Neighbours China and Pakistan (8 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 34 Questions)

typology.description: Exhibit memory of previously learned material by recalling macroeconomic facts, terminology, economic concepts, and historical reform milestones.
Solve economic problems to new situations by applying acquired knowledge, national income formulas, multiplier equations, and fiscal tools.
Examine economic trends, analyze comparative development indicators across nations, make inferences, and propose developmental policies.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including data tables, graphs, and news extracts.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% provided across sections.

prescribed_books.title: Introductory Macroeconomics, Class XII
Indian Economic Development, Class XII

breakdown.details: Independent analytical study on an economic topic (e.g. Monetary Policy, GST, Digital Currency, Make in India).
Viva on project methodology, data sources, and analytical conclusions with an external examiner.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Evaluated jointly by internal and external examiners.

editorial_study_tips: In National Income numericals, clearly write out the intermediate equations (e.g. GDPmp to NNPfc) before inserting numerical values.
In Indian Economic Development, memorize landmark policy years (e.g., Planning Commission 1950, NEP 1991, NITI Aayog 2015) for precise MCQs.
Draw clear, labeled macroeconomic equilibrium graphs (AD-AS and Investment-Saving curves) when explaining inflationary/deflationary gaps.

subject: History
title: CBSE Class 12 History Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Themes in Indian History (Part I: Ancient Archaeology & Early States; Part II: Agrarian Relations, Mughal Court, Bhakti-Sufi Traditions; Part III: Colonialism, 1857 Revolt, Mahatma Gandhi & the Nationalist Movement, Making of the Constitution).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 History explores Indian history chronologically through key themes: Ancient Harappan urbanism and early states, Medieval court chronicles and devotional movements, and Modern colonial encounters and the nationalist movement.

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part-I (Ancient)
chapters: Theme 1: Bricks, Beads and Bones (The Harappan Civilisation)
Theme 2: Kings, Farmers and Towns (Early States and Economies)
Theme 3: Kinship, Caste and Class (Early Societies)
Theme 4: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings (Cultural Developments: Buddhism & Jainism)

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part-II (Medieval)
chapters: Theme 5: Through the Eyes of Travellers
Theme 6: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
Theme 7: An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara
Theme 8: Peasants, Zamindars and the State (Agrarian Society & Mughal Empire)

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part-III (Modern)
chapters: Theme 9: Colonialism and the Countryside
Theme 10: Rebels and the Raj (1857 Revolt)
Theme 11: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
Theme 12: Framing the Constitution (The Beginning of a New Era)

units.name: Map Identification & Location
chapters: Significant historical sites across Ancient, Medieval, and Modern themes (5 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 34 Questions)

typology.description: 21 Objective MCQs of 1 mark each covering Part I (7), Part II (7), and Part III (7).
6 Short Answer questions of 3 marks each (2 from each part, 100-150 words).
3 Long Answer essay questions of 8 marks each (1 from each part, with internal choice).
3 Source-based passage questions of 4 marks each (1 from each part, with sub-questions).
1 Map-based question of 5 marks (identification, location, and labelling of significant historical sites).

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency questions including direct analysis of textual and epigraphic sources.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% provided across short and long answer questions.

prescribed_books.title: Themes in Indian History Part I
Themes in Indian History Part II
Themes in Indian History Part III

breakdown.details: Investigation of an archaeological site, monument, movement, or historical personality with primary evidence.
Oral defense with CBSE external examiner discussing historical methodology and sources.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Project must integrate primary sources (inscriptions, coins, oral histories, travelogues).

editorial_study_tips: Source-based passages carry 12 marks; practice answering questions directly from the boxed extracts in the NCERT textbook.
Maintain timeline charts for Theme 11 (Nationalist Movement) to ensure chronological accuracy in 8-mark long essays.
Practice official map locations (e.g., Lothal, Sanchi, Vijayanagara, Dandi, Champaran) repeatedly on blank outline maps.

subject: Political Science
title: CBSE Class 12 Political Science Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Part A: Contemporary World Politics (Bipolarity, New Centres of Power, South Asia, International Organizations, Globalization). Part B: Politics in India since Independence (Nation-Building, Planned Development, Democratic Resurgence, Recent Developments).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 Political Science examines international relations post-Cold War and the political evolution of democratic India from nation-building to contemporary coalition and development politics.

units.name: Contemporary World Politics
chapters: The End of Bipolarity (6 marks)
Contemporary Centres of Power: European Union, ASEAN, China, Japan, Korea (6 marks)
Contemporary South Asia (6 marks)
International Organizations (6 marks)
Security in the Contemporary World (6 marks)
Environment and Natural Resources (6 marks)
Globalization (4 marks)

units.name: Politics in India Since Independence
chapters: Challenges of Nation-Building: Integration of princely states, linguistic reorganization (6 marks)
Era of One-Party Dominance (4 marks)
Politics of Planned Development: Five-year plans, Green Revolution (4 marks)
India's External Relations: Non-alignment, wars with China/Pakistan, nuclear policy (6 marks)
Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System (4 marks)
The Crisis of Democratic Order: Emergency 1975, aftermath (6 marks)
Regional Aspirations: Kashmir, Punjab, North-East accords (4 marks)
Recent Developments in Indian Politics: Coalition era, NDA/UPA policies, contemporary issues (6 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 30 Questions)

typology.description: Define geopolitical terms, recall treaty dates, identify international bodies, and summarize political events.
Examine foreign policy motivations, analyze democratic crises, and interpret political cartoons/maps.
Passage-based, cartoon-based, and map-based interpretive questions (12 marks) plus essay evaluations.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: 50% competency-focused questions including cartoon interpretations, map questions, and policy passage analyses.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of approximately 33% provided across short and essay-type questions.

prescribed_books.title: Contemporary World Politics, Class XII
Politics in India Since Independence, Class XII

breakdown.details: Research report on a contemporary geopolitical issue, Indian election, or foreign policy initiative.
Oral viva with external examiner assessing subject knowledge and critical thinking.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Evaluated jointly by internal and external examiners appointed by CBSE.

editorial_study_tips: Review every political cartoon in both NCERT textbooks; cartoon-based questions appear regularly and carry 4 to 6 marks.
Organize foreign policy treaties and UN agencies in a tabular format with headquarters, founding years, and principal mandates.
Structure long answers on the Emergency and Coalition Politics with neutral, constitutional arguments based strictly on textbook analysis.

subject: English Core
title: CBSE Class 12 English Core Syllabus (2026-27)
description: Official CBSE Senior Secondary curriculum document (covering Classes XI & XII); presenting Class XII board syllabus: Section A: Reading Skills (Unseen Passages); Section B: Creative Writing Skills (Notices, Invitations, Letters, Articles/Reports); Section C: Literature Textbooks (Flamingo and Vistas).
course_structure_overview: CBSE Class 12 English Core develops advanced reading comprehension, formal administrative writing, and nuanced textual analysis of modern prose and poetry.

units.name: Reading Skills
chapters: One unseen passage to assess comprehension, interpretation, analysis and vocabulary (12 marks)
One unseen case-based factual passage with visual input/charts (10 marks)

units.name: Creative Writing Skills
chapters: Notice Writing (up to 50 words, 4 marks)
Formal/Informal Invitation and Reply (up to 50 words, 4 marks)
Letter to the Editor / Application for a Job with Bio-data (120-150 words, 5 marks)
Article / Report Writing on contemporary issues (120-150 words, 5 marks)

units.name: Literature Textbooks and Supplementary Reading
chapters: Flamingo: One Poetry extract (6 marks) + One Prose extract (6 marks)
Flamingo: Five Short Answer Questions (5 x 2 = 10 marks)
Vistas: Two Short Answer Questions (2 x 2 = 4 marks)
Flamingo: One Long Answer Question (5 marks)
Vistas: One Long Answer Question (5 marks)

question_paper_design.format: Theory Written Paper (80 Marks, 3 Hours, 13 Questions)

typology.description: Evaluating inference, tone, vocabulary in context, and data synthesis from unseen texts.
Format adherence, logical organization of ideas, formal register, and grammatical precision.
Appreciation of poetic devices, character motivation, socio-historical context, and moral dilemmas.

question_paper_design.competency_focus: High focus on inferential reading questions and thematic extrapolations from literature.
question_paper_design.choice_pattern: Internal choices of 100% provided within each writing skill item and designated literature questions.

prescribed_books.title: Flamingo: English Reader, Class XII
Vistas: Supplementary Reader, Class XII

breakdown.details: Audio comprehension and response recording.
Oral monologue, role-play, or project presentation.
Thematic essay, interview transcription, or literary critique portfolio.

practical_guidance.guidelines: Evaluated at school level based on CBSE ALS speaking/listening bands.

editorial_study_tips: Draw a clean box around Notices and Invitations; marks are deducted if the enclosing box is omitted.
In Job Applications, ensure your Bio-Data includes distinct headings: Personal Details, Educational Qualifications in tabular format, Work Experience, and References.
Memorize poetic devices (metaphor, simile, irony, transferred epithet) for all Flamingo poems (My Mother at Sixty-Six, Keeping Quiet, A Thing of Beauty, A Roadside Stand, Aunt Jennifer's Tigers).
